description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
Random init; prints the task's public attributes and example I/O to learn the format.
No LayerNorm. Attention reads the prompt only and sums thermometer codes into cumulative counts; 20 ReLUs threshold counts against the step counter; head takes differences to get a one-hot digit.
As ThermoCountStepMLP but one ReLU per threshold: shortfall relu(c-count) with a penalty head, so argmax picks the smallest digit with zero shortfall.
No MLP, no LayerNorm. Head logit[d] = sum_{j<d}(c - 1/2 - count(<=j)); partial sums are concave in d and peak at the c-th smallest digit, so the final argmax does the thresholding.

d_model=vocab, identity head. Digits embed as hinge curves, attention sums the prompt's curves, position adds the slope: logit[d] is the negative pinball loss of d, whose minimiser is the c-th smallest digit.
PinballLogitSpace with every curve doubled, so all weights are integers (hinges -2 max(d-a,0), slope 2c+1). Adds min decision margin to the exhaustive check.
W_q=W_k=0: attention is a plain mean of all tokens seen, so the model is linear up to the final argmax. Emitted digits lie at or below the target, so they only shift the pinball slope.
Fixes UniformAttentionLinear: the mean also averages answer-position embeddings, so the slopes are solved recursively. Attention is a plain mean, so the model is linear up to the final argmax.
Attention replaced by its parameter-free equivalent, a causal mean of the tokens so far. All parameters are now token_emb, pos_emb and an identity head.
CausalMeanNoAttentionParams without the identity head: the hidden state is the logit vector, leaving only token_emb and pos_emb as parameters.
CausalMeanNoHead with position factored into one scalar slope per step times a shared direction, replacing the 16x11 position table.

No position embedding. The causal mean's 1/T normaliser acts as the step counter: fixed token slopes become step-dependent once the output is rescaled by T = 5 + c. Only token_emb and W_v are parameters.

Unmodified 64-dim, 4-head, 3-layer architecture with LayerNorm. Slack dims give each digit zero mean and equal norm so LayerNorm is a constant rescale undone by W_o; one head does the work and everything else is zero.
StockArchPinball cut to its working part: 14 dims, one head, one block, no MLP, LayerNorm kept. A smaller answer flag (100, not 1000) should widen the margin.
PinballIntegerWeights with answer flag M=5 instead of 10 (attention score -7.5): sharpness sweep, how soft can prompt-only attention get?
Sharpness sweep: answer flag M=3 (attention score -2.7), so each answer token keeps about 7% of a prompt token's attention weight.
Sharpness sweep: answer flag M=4 (attention score -4.8), locating the failure point between M=5 (exact) and M=3 (8% exhaustive).
Robustness probe: PinballIntegerWeights plus seeded Gaussian noise with std 0.02 on every parameter.

Real gated attention reduced to its working part: query and key are the flag scalar, values are x, so the four attention matrices become two scalars (score scale and output gain). No head; identity logits.
ScalarFlagAttention with the same seeded std 0.02 noise that took the full-matrix version to 0.7% exhaustive: tests whether the attention matrices caused that fragility.
Noise sweep on ScalarFlagAttention: seeded std 0.06, roughly where the summed logit noise should approach the unit margin.
ScalarFlagAttention with all curves multiplied by 10 under the same seeded std 0.06 noise: is the noise limit just a matter of weight scale?
ScaledCurvesK10Noise006 with attention score scale 0.12 instead of 0.3, testing whether the leftover errors come from noisy flags skewing the prompt attention weights.
Negative control: slope 2c-1, which ignores the previous token's residual curve. Should stall by re-emitting the previous digit.
ScalarFlagAttention plus rank-one position: one integer per step, 2c+1, sets the quantile on the digit dims and doubles as the prompt/answer attention flag. No separate flag constant.
Truly autoregressive: one attention head sums the prompt curves and another subtracts the emitted digits, so each step finds the minimum of what remains with a step-independent slope.
SlopeIsFlag under std 0.02 noise on 5 seeds, checked exhaustively; the logged accuracy is seed 0. Part of a same-seeds comparison of the three main designs.
ScalarFlagAttention under std 0.02 noise on the same 5 seeds, checked exhaustively; the logged accuracy is seed 0. Checks whether the earlier single-seed 100% was representative.
Full W_q/W_k/W_v/W_o attention matrices under std 0.02 noise on the same 5 seeds, identity logits; the logged accuracy is seed 0. Tests the claim that those matrices cause the noise fragility.
